messages:
Alex: Support escalated — Acme seeing p95 and some 504s right after the runtime rollout at ~14:00 UTC. Ticket SUP-4821.
Maria: grabbing telemetry -> <https://console.redwood/metrics/acme/rollout/roll-2026-03-17-336>
Maria: p95 jumped from ~160ms to ~380ms in the canary window after roll-2026-03-17-336
deploy-bot: Deployment roll-2026-03-17-336 started by @Maria at 2026-03-17T14:00:05Z
Support: customers report requests timing out, intermittent 504s, especially on chat endpoints
Anya: checking logs — backend app latency stable; nginx 504s line up with long waits inside runtime hotpath
Dan: that pattern suggests queueing / tail latency, not upstream slowness. Any change to scheduler or cache?
Maria: KV cache miss rate for tenant acme increased coincident with the spike. also seeing scheduler warnings
Anya: found warnings in runtime log:
```
WARN scheduler/refill.go: refill loop lag tenant=acme backlog=96 iter=7
```
Dan: note we merged a per-tenant burst/fair-share scheduler change in this rollout. burst token checks are more expensive now.
Alex: what is Acme's tenant config? could be interacting badly
Support: forwarded tenant config — burst=600, sustained=150
Anya: that high burst plus the new slow refill path could cause hotspots and extra KV ops (misses) — more work per request -> queueing
Maria: mitigation options without full rollback:
- pin tenant to previous runtime binary
- reduce tenant burst via billing API
- route tenant to a dedicated pool (if available)
- temporary autoscaling bump for canary nodes
Dan: can we pin quickly? that's the fastest customer-side mitigation
Maria: executing: `redwood pin-runtime --tenant acme --version v1.12.2-stable`
deploy-bot: Pin request accepted; routing updated at 2026-03-17T14:12:42Z
Alex: monitoring metrics... p95 is dropping back toward ~210ms after the pin
Support: telling customer we applied a workaround and are monitoring, they asked for ETA on root cause
Anya: I'll diff the rollout changes focusing on scheduler and kv_cache modules. suspect expensive path introduced in scheduler refill logic
Dan: I'll script a canary bisect: roll back scheduler change in small chunks across canary nodes to isolate the offending commit
Maria: still a handful of 504s but much reduced. logging shows KV hit rate recovering for acme
Alex: documented repro/observations in the support ticket:
- Spike observed at ~2026-03-17T14:02 after roll-2026-03-17-336
- KV cache misses rose for tenant acme
- Scheduler refill warnings present in runtime logs
- Temporary mitigation: pinned acme to v1.12.2-stable at 14:12
- Next: automated canary bisect, targeted rollback for scheduler refill optimization
Dan: creating bisect runbook and will tag eng-runtime + eng-sre for on-call followup
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0317-99, priority=P2
Maria: Opening a postmortem ticket and assigning to eng-runtime. Proposed long-term fixes: make refill loop backoff resilient, add a telemetry guard to revert expensive path when KV miss amplification is detected, and add tenant-config safety checks during rollout.
Alex: great work. I'll close the loop with the customer in 30m if stable. Please shout if it regresses. :thumbsup:
